description.ncbi_summary: The protein encoded by this gene is a member of the keratin gene family. The keratins are intermediate filament proteins responsible for the structural integrity of epithelial cells and are subdivided into cytokeratins and hair keratins. Most of the type I cytokeratins consist of acidic proteins which are arranged in pairs of heterotypic keratin chains and are clustered in a region on chromosome 17q21.2. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Structural component of intermediate filaments in the epithelium. Forms heteropolymers with type II keratin KRT5, assembling into keratin intermediate filament network that promotes mechanical resilience of undifferentiated cells, including hair follicle bulge cells, foregut basal progenitors and intestinal crypt cells. Displays an antagonist role with KRT14 in basal epithelial cells, where KRT14 promotes cell differentiation while KRT15 maintains the progenitor state and promotes proliferation and clonogenicity (PubMed:41511042). Promotes the progenitor state in basal keratinocytes by maintaining cytoplasmic YAP1 less effectively than KRT14 due to missing biochemical motifs, thereby allowing higher YAP1 nuclear activity (PubMed:41511042). Also contributes to epithelial cell regeneration after injury. In the absence of KRT14, forms a bona fide, but ultrastructurally distinct keratin filament network with KRT5 (By similarity).
